To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) T cells from patients affected by SLE proliferate in response to anti‐CD3 stimulation, but require a costimulatory signal provided by B7/BBI antigen; and 2) T cell proliferation is similar to that of normal individuals.

the T cell proliferation in patients with S LE is normal in the absence of a second costimulatory signal and is enhanced in the presence of the B7/ BB1 molecule, suggesting that the T cells from patients are not intrinsically unresponsive to the costimulatory signals.
the T cell proliferative response to anti‐CD3 plus B7/BB 1 is not intrinsicaly impaired in patients with systemic erythematosus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that regulate the immune system in health and disease.
the role of B7/CD28 costimulatory pathway in the regulation of T cell activation in SLE.
the molecular basis of T cell activation, and in particular with the role of the B7/ BB1 costimulatory molecule in the pathogenesis of autoimmune diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
T cell proliferation via TCR/CD28 costimulation is not defective in SLE, but that the B7/ BB1 molecule is probably involved in the pathogenesis of SLE.
the CD3/CD28 costimulation pathway appears to be intact in SLE.
T cells from patients and normal subjects respond equally well to stimulation with anti‐CD3 and B7/1 costimulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the B7/ BB1 molecule plays an essential costimulatory role in CD3‐mediation of T cell activation in patients with S LE.
the B7/ BB1 costimulation is intact in T cells from SLE patients, but the B7/1BB1 antigen is not expressed by the APCs in SLE patients.
the B7/CD28 costimulatory pathway is intact in SLE T cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the B7 costimulatory pathway is not intrinsicaly defective in SLE patients, and therefore, it is unlikely that this pathway is involved in the pathogenesis of this autoimmune disease.
